How embedding models work - Example Blog

How embedding models turn text into numbers. An embedding model reads a piece of text and produces a list of numbers, called a vector, that captures its meaning. Texts with similar meaning end up with vectors that point in similar directions, which is why search systems compare vectors with cosine similarity instead of matching keywords.

Why dimensions matter. A model such as MiniLM produces 384 numbers per text, while larger models produce 1024 or more. More dimensions can hold more nuance but cost more storage and more time to compare. A store with one hundred thousand chunks at 1024 dimensions in 32 bit floats needs about 410 megabytes for the vectors alone.

Queries and documents. Several models expect a short instruction in front of the query, such as Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages, and no prefix on the documents. Skipping the prefix quietly lowers retrieval quality. Reranking then re-scores the top results with a slower, more accurate model that reads the query and each passage together.

Practical advice. Measure retrieval quality on your own questions before changing models, keep the embedding model fixed for a whole index, and re-embed everything when you switch. Store the model name and version next to each vector so a mismatch is detectable.
